ud2.5:0.2: The Discourse about the Lay Follower
ud2.5:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud2.5:1.3: Then at that time a certain lay follower from Icchānaṅgala had arrived at Sāvatthī with some business or other.
ud2.5:1.4: Then that lay follower, having concluded that business in Sāvatthī, went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side.
ud2.5:1.5: While sat on one side the Fortunate One said this to that lay follower:
ud2.5:1.6: “At long last, lay follower, you have made arrangements, so to say, for coming here.”
ud2.5:2.1: “For a long time, reverend Sir, I have desired to come to see the Fortunate One, but I have been engaged with some sort of duty and business or another, and I have thus been unable to come to see the Fortunate One.”
ud2.5:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud2.5:4.1: “For he who has nothing there is happiness indeed,
ud2.5:4.2: For the one who has discerned the Dhamma, for the learned,
ud2.5:4.3: See how one who has something is troubled,
ud2.5:4.4: He is a person who is in a state of bondage in regard to (other) people.”
